subject: maths
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 2½ hours · Maximum marks: 85 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–17 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 18–27 have two parts of 1 mark each; question 28 is a case study with five 1-mark questions.
Section B: questions 29–37 carry 2 marks, 38–42 carry 3 marks and 43–44 carry 5 marks.
Every answer shows the working. Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The HCF of 3³ × 5 and 3² × 5² is —
questions.work:
HCF takes each common prime factor with its lowest power.
Power of 3: lower of 3 and 2 → 3²; power of 5: lower of 1 and 2 → 5¹.
HCF = 3² × 5 = 9 × 5 = 45.

questions.q: The pair kx + 2y = 5 and 3x + y = 1 has no solution when k is —
questions.work:
No solution means parallel lines: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂.
k/3 = 2/1 ⇒ k = 6.
Check c₁/c₂ = 5/1 = 5 ≠ 2, so the lines are parallel, not the same. k = 6.

questions.q: The sum of a number and its reciprocal is 5/2. The number is —
If 2p + 1, 13 and 5p − 3 are in A.P., then p is —
questions.work:
In an A.P. the middle term is the average: 2 × 13 = (2p + 1) + (5p − 3).
26 = 7p − 2 ⇒ 7p = 28 ⇒ p = 4.

questions.q: The cost price of 10 articles equals the selling price of 8 articles. The gain or loss percent is —
questions.work:
Let C.P. of one article = ₹1; then C.P. of 10 = ₹10 = S.P. of 8, so S.P. of one = 10/8 = ₹1.25.
Gain = 0.25 on 1 ⇒ 25% gain.

questions.q: A fan costs ₹1,500 cash or ₹360 down + 3 monthly instalments of ₹390. The interest charged is —
questions.work:
Balance = 1500 − 360 = ₹1,140.
Instalments total 3 × 390 = ₹1,170.
Interest = 1170 − 1140 = ₹30.

questions.q: For a cyclic quadrilateral, which is true?
options: One opposite angle is always obtuse
questions.work: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180° — they are supplementary.

questions.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 110°. Then ∠C is —
From a point P, 5 cm from the centre of a circle, the tangent is 4 cm long. The radius is —
A triangle ABC with BC = 3 cm, ∠C = 30° and AB − AC = 3.2 cm —
questions.work:
By the triangle inequality AB < AC + BC, i.e. AB − AC < BC.
Here AB − AC = 3.2 cm is not less than BC = 3 cm, so no such triangle exists.

cosec²67° − tan²23° + 1 is —
questions.work:
cosec 67° = sec(90° − 67°) = sec 23°.
sec²23° − tan²23° = 1, so the value is 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.q: If cos θ × (1/sec θ) = 1 and θ is acute or zero, then θ is —
questions.work: 1/sec θ = cos θ, so cos²θ = 1 ⇒ cos θ = 1 ⇒ θ = 0°.

questions.q: If the mean of 6, 7, p, 8, q, 14 is 9, then —
Which of the following cannot be a probability?
questions.work: 5/4 is greater than 1, and no probability can exceed 1.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) (x + y)² − (x − y)² = 4xy. (ii) The HCF of 6x²y and 9xy² is 3x²y².
questions.answer:
(i) True: (x² + 2xy + y²) − (x² − 2xy + y²) = 4xy.
(ii) False: HCF of 6 and 9 is 3; lowest powers are x¹ and y¹, so HCF = 3xy.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The solution of 3x + 4y = 17 and 4x − 3y = 6 is x = ____, y = ____. (ii) The line 3x − 2y = 12 cuts the x-axis at ____.
Match: (i) If (α − 3)x² + 4(α − 3)x + 4 = 0 has equal real roots, α = ____ (ii) If x = ½ is a root of x² + kx − 5/4 = 0, k = ____ — (A) 3 and 4 (B) 4 (C) 2 (D) 6
questions.answer:
(i) D = 16(α − 3)² − 16(α − 3) = 16(α − 3)(α − 4) = 0 ⇒ α = 3 or 4. α = 3 makes the x² term vanish (not a quadratic), so α = 4 → (B); the paper's key offers (A) '3 and 4'.
(ii) ¼ + k/2 − 5/4 = 0 ⇒ k/2 = 1 ⇒ k = 2 → (C).

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) R(−2, −3) lies in quadrant III. (ii) The point (0, 5) lies on the x-axis.
questions.answer:
(i) True: both coordinates are negative.
(ii) False: x = 0, so it lies on the y-axis.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The area of a parallelogram of area 18 cm² on a base of 6 cm has height ____. (ii) The area of an isosceles triangle with base 12 cm and equal sides 10 cm is ____.
questions.answer:
(i) Height = area ÷ base = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 cm.
(ii) Height = √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm; area = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm².

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The volume of a cube of surface area 150 cm² is ____. (ii) A cone and a cylinder with equal radii have equal curved surfaces; slant height of cone : height of cylinder = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) 6a² = 150 ⇒ a = 5 ⇒ V = 125 cm³.
(ii) πrl = 2πrh ⇒ l = 2h ⇒ l : h = 2 : 1.

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) sin 10θ = cos 8θ (10θ acute) gives tan 9θ = 1. (ii) The value of sin A can be 4/3.
questions.answer:
(i) True: 10θ + 8θ = 90° ⇒ θ = 5° ⇒ tan 45° = 1.
(ii) False: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse ≤ 1.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) A kite string 20√3 m long makes 60° with the ground; the kite's height is ____. (ii) A tower casts its shadow 15 m from its foot at an elevation of 60°; its height is ____.
Write True or False: (i) Class mark is a measure of central tendency. (ii) The median of 3, 1, 5, 2, 4 is 5.
questions.answer:
(i) False: mean, median and mode are; a class mark is just a class's midpoint.
(ii) False: in order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 the middle value is 3.

questions.q: A box has 4 red balls, 5 white balls and some green balls. The probability of a red ball is 1/5. Fill in: (i) P(green) = ____ (ii) P(not green) = ____.

sections.title: Case study: read the information and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: The speed of the boat upstream is —
questions.work: Going against the stream, the stream slows the boat: 18 − x.

questions.q: The equation that describes the situation is —
The speed of the stream is —
questions.work:
x² + 48x − 324 = (x + 54)(x − 6) = 0 ⇒ x = 6 or −54.
Speed cannot be negative, so x = 6 km/h.

questions.q: The time taken downstream is —
questions.work:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h; time = 24 ÷ 24 = 1 hour = 60 minutes.
(Upstream: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 hours, one hour more ✓.)

questions.q: The relation used for time is —
questions.work: Distance = speed × time, so time = distance ÷ speed.

sections.passage: A motorboat whose speed in still water is 18 km/h takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Let the speed of the stream be x km/h.

questions.q: If a + 1/a = 2, find a³ + 1/a³.
The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 20 m and its length is 4 m more than its breadth. Find its length, breadth and area.
questions.answer:
Let breadth = b, length = b + 4.
2(l + b) = 20 ⇒ (b + 4) + b = 10 ⇒ 2b = 6 ⇒ b = 3.
Length = 7 m, breadth = 3 m, area = 7 × 3 = 21 m².

questions.q: Find a natural number whose square diminished by 84 equals three times 8 more than the number.
For an A.P. with a = −5 and d = 4, find the sum of the first 40 terms.
Three metal cubes of edges 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm are melted into one cube. Find its edge.
Prove that (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)/(1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ) = 1.
questions.answer:
sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)² − 2 sin²θ cos²θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ.
So the fraction equals 1.

questions.q: A bag contains 5 red, 4 black and 3 green balls. One is drawn at random. Find the probability of (i) a red or green ball (ii) a ball which is not red.
Divide 16 into two parts such that twice the square of the larger part exceeds the square of the smaller part by 164.
questions.answer:
Let the larger part be x; the smaller is 16 − x.
2x² − (16 − x)² = 164 ⇒ 2x² − (256 − 32x + x²) = 164
⇒ x² + 32x − 420 = 0 ⇒ (x + 42)(x − 10) = 0 ⇒ x = 10.
The parts are 10 and 6. Check: 2 × 100 − 36 = 164 ✓.

or.q: Ramu's age two years ago multiplied by his age five years from now gives 120. Find his present age.
or.answer:
Let the present age be x.
(x − 2)(x + 5) = 120 ⇒ x² + 3x − 10 = 120 ⇒ x² + 3x − 130 = 0.
(x + 13)(x − 10) = 0 ⇒ x = 10 (age cannot be negative).
Ramu is 10 years old.

questions.q: A washing machine is available for ₹13,500 cash or ₹6,500 cash down followed by three monthly instalments of ₹2,500. Find the rate of interest.
Construct △ABC in which BC = 4 cm, ∠B = 60° and AB − AC = 1.2 cm.
questions.answer:
1. Draw BC = 4 cm.
2. At B make ∠CBX = 60°.
3. Cut BD = 1.2 cm on BX.
4. Join DC and draw its perpendicular bisector, meeting BX produced at A.
5. Join AC. △ABC is the required triangle (AD = AC, so AB − AC = BD = 1.2 cm).

questions.q: A conical tent is 6 m high with base radius 8 m. Find (i) its slant height (ii) the cloth needed (iii) its volume.
A pair of dice is thrown once. Find the probability of (i) the same number on both (ii) an odd prime as the sum.
Find the sum of all three-digit numbers which leave remainder 2 when divided by 5.
Prove that the angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.
questions.answer:
Given: arc AB of a circle with centre O; C is a point on the remaining part.
To prove: ∠AOB = 2∠ACB.
Construction: join CO and produce it to a point D.
Proof: in △OAC, OA = OC (radii), so ∠OAC = ∠OCA.
The exterior angle ∠AOD = ∠OAC + ∠OCA = 2∠OCA …(1)
Similarly in △OBC, ∠BOD = 2∠OCB …(2)
Adding (1) and (2): ∠AOD + ∠BOD = 2(∠OCA + ∠OCB), i.e. ∠AOB = 2∠ACB. Proved.
(For a major arc, the same steps give reflex ∠AOB = 2∠ACB.)
